items.abstract: <jats:p>Generating production-grade Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) code using Large Language Models (LLMs) presents a critical challenge: ensuring the determinism and safety required for industrial environments. Current baseline prompting methods, such as Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), Chain-of-Code (CoC), and Contrastive CoT (CCoT), often yield fragmented results that lack the structural integrity needed for safety-critical IEC 61131-3 synthesis. This paper introduces CoT+ (Chain-of-Thought Extended), a unified prompting architecture that integrates these four paradigms into a deterministic, multi-stage pipeline.The novelty of this research lies in its rigorous three-layer validation framework, utilizing Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), LLM-in-the-Loop (LITL), and Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score analysis. To provide "double justification" for the superiority of CoT+, we employ an advanced Inter-Rater Reliability (IRR) assessment using Cohen’s (κ) for pairwise agreement and Krippendorff’s (α) for multi-rater consistency. This dual-layered statistical approach ensures that performance gains are not only observable across lexical and semantic layers but are also mathematically robust and validator-agnostic. Our results demonstrate that CoT+ achieves significantly higher safety compliance and cross-validator stability than existing baselines. This research contributes: (i) a deployment-oriented prompting template for industrial PLC synthesis, and (ii) a fully reproducible, IRR-qualified validation methodology designed for external verification in safety-critical domains.</jats:p>
title: CoT+ (Chain-of-Thought Extended): A Reproducible Multi-Reasoning Prompting Architecture for Deterministic PLC Code Generation

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has revolutionized reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling them to tackle complex tasks by mimicking step-by-step human thought processes. However, traditional CoT methods often suffer from high computational costs and context dilution, limiting their effectiveness, particularly in resource-constrained or real-time applications. To address these challenges, we introduce
                    <jats:bold>Dynamic Recursive Chain-of-Thought (DR-CoT)</jats:bold>
                    , a novel reasoning framework for parameter-efficient models. DR-CoT synergistically integrates recursive reasoning, dynamic context truncation, and a voting mechanism. By selectively retaining the most salient context within a fixed token budget and aggregating inferences from multiple independent reasoning chains, DR-CoT significantly enhances reasoning accuracy. Extensive evaluations on challenging reasoning benchmarks, including GPQA Diamond and AIME2024, demonstrate the efficacy of DR-CoT. On GPQA Diamond, DR-CoT sees Pass@1 accuracy gains of 1.5% for , 2.7% for Grok 3 Beta, and 4.4% for . Similarly, AIME2024 results reveal consistent improvements of 3-4 percentage points across evaluated models. Furthermore, DR-CoT enhances zero-shot classification performance on GPQA Diamond, enabling compact BERT-sized models to surpass larger language models such as  and . In code generation tasks using HumanEval, DRCoT empowers models to exceed the performance of established frontier LLMs, including , , and . These comprehensive results underscore DR-CoT’s effectiveness in bridging the performance gap between parameter-efficient models and state-of-the-art LLMs across multiple domains.
                  </jats:p>
title: DR-CoT: dynamic recursive chain of thought with meta reasoning for parameter efficient models
